questions.q: A parallel beam of light is allowed to fall on a transparent spherical globe of diameter $30$ cm and refractive index $1 . 5$. The distance from the centre of the globe at which beam of light can converge is _____~$mm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the refraction at the left surface,& $u = - \infty , R = + 15cm$.

$\dfrac{\mu2}{v} - \dfrac{\mu1}{u} = \dfrac{{μ}_{2} - {μ}_{1}}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 . 5}{v1} - \dfrac{1}{- \infty} = \dfrac{1 . 5 - 1}{+ 15}$

$⇒ {v}_{1} = 45cm$

For the refraction at the right~surface,~$u = 45 - 30 = 15cm, R = - 15cm$

$\dfrac{\mu2}{v} - \dfrac{\mu1}{u} = \dfrac{{μ}_{2} - {μ}_{1}}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v2} - \dfrac{1 . 5}{15} = \dfrac{1 - 1 . 5}{- 15}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = 7 . 5cm$

Therefore, the distance from the centre where the beam will converge is,

$15 + 7 . 5 = 22 . 5cm = 225mm$

questions.q: A pole is vertically submerged in swimming pool, such that it gives a length of shadow $2 . 15m$ within water when sunlight is incident at an angle of $30 °$ with the surface of water. If swimming pool is filled to a height of $1 . 5m,$ then the height of the pole above the water surface in centimeters is~$( {n}_{w} = \dfrac{4}{3} ) ________ .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let angle& $BAC$~is~$\theta$.

Applying Snell's law at $E$, we get~$1 \times sin60 ° = \dfrac{4}{3} \times sin\theta$

$⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{8} ⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{sin\theta}{1 - \left(sin\theta\right)2} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{37}$

Now,~$BC = 1 . 5 \times tan\theta = 1 . 28$

Then,~$AB = 2 . 15 - BC = 0 . 86m$

Required value,~$DF = ABtan30 ° = 0 . 5015m \approx 50cm$

questions.q: Cross-section view of a prism is the equilateral triangle $ABC$ shown in the figure. The minimum deviation is observed using this prism when the angle of incidence is equal to the prism angle. The time taken by light to travel from $P$ (midpoint of $BC$) to $A$ is~___________~$\times {10}^{- 10}s .$~(Given, speed of light in vacuum $= 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$ and $cos30 ° = \dfrac{3}{2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${δ}_\min = 2i - A$
$A = 2i - A$
$A = i$
$\mu = \dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{{δ}_\min + A}{2}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{sin ( A )}{sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{sin60 °}{sin30 °}$
$\mu = \sqrt{3}$
$v = \dfrac{c}{μ} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{3}ms^{- 1}$
$t = \dfrac{AP}{v} = 5\sqrt{3} \times {10}^{- 2}\left(\dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{3}\right) = 5 \times {10}^{- 10}\text{s}$
So, $x = 5$

questions.q: In an experiment for estimating the value of focal length of converging mirror, image of an object placed at $40$ cm from the pole of the mirror is formed at distance $120$ cm from the pole of the mirror. These distances are measured with a modified scale in which there are $20$ small divisions in $1$ cm. The value of error in measurement of focal length of the mirror is $\dfrac{1}{K}cm$. The value of $K$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $u = - 40cm, v = - 120cm$

Using mirror formula,~$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

~$\dfrac{- 1}{120} - \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{f} ⇒ f = - 30cm$

Now, differentiating mirror equation, we get

$\dfrac{- 1}{v2}dv - \dfrac{1}{u2}du = - \dfrac{1}{f2}df$

Also, the least count of scale,~$dv = du = \dfrac{1}{20}cm$

Putting in above equation,~

$∴ \dfrac{120}{( 120{)}^{2}} + \dfrac{120}{( 40{)}^{2}} = \dfrac{df}{( 30{)}^{2}}$

On solving, we get

$df = \dfrac{1}{32}cm$

$∴ K = 32$.

questions.q: Two immiscible liquids of refractive indices $\dfrac{8}{5}$ and $\dfrac{3}{2}$ respectively are put in a beaker as shown in the figure. The height of each column is $6$ cm. A coin is placed at the bottom of the beaker. For near normal vision, the apparent depth of the coin is $\dfrac{α}{4}cm$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the apparent height of the coin when seen through the combination of liquids can be written as

${h}_{app} = \dfrac{h1}{\mu1} + \dfrac{h2}{\mu2} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

\begin{cases}{h}_{app}$& = & $\dfrac{6}{3 / 2} + \dfrac{6}{8 / 5}$cm \\ & = & 4 + $\dfrac{15}{4}$cm \\ & = & $\dfrac{31}{4}$cm\end{cases}$

Hence, $\alpha =31.

$

questions.q:
The graph between $\dfrac{1}{u}$ and $\dfrac{1}{v}$ for a thin convex lens in order to determine its focal length is plotted as shown in the figure. The refractive index of lens~is $1 . 5$~and its both the surfaces have same radius of curvatures $R$. The value of $R$ will be _____ $cm$.

(Where $u =$ object distance, $v =$ image distance)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

For point $B, \dfrac{1}{u} = - 0 . 10{cm}^{- 1}, \dfrac{1}{v} = 0$

$∴$ Thus, $u = - 10cm, v = \infty$

Using lens formula,~

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = 0 - \left(-10\right)$

$⇒ f = 10cm$

Now, using Lens maker's formula,~

\dfrac{1}{f} =\left(\mu -1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R1} - \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}}\right),where,~$\mu$~is refractive index of lens.

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{10cm} = \left($1 . 5 - 1\$right)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right) = \dfrac{1}{R}$⇒ R = 10cm$

$

questions.q: A thin cylindrical rod of length $10$ cm is placed horizontally on the principle axis of a concave mirror of focal length $20$ cm. The rod is placed in a such a way that mid point of the rod is at $40$ cm from the pole of mirror. The length of the image formed by the mirror will be~$\dfrac{x}{3}cm$.~The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As per sign conventions, object distance& ${u}_{A} = - 45cm$, focal length~$f = - 20cm$.

From the mirror formula

$\dfrac{1}{vA} + \dfrac{1}{uA} = \dfrac{1}{f} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{vA} + \dfrac{1}{- 45} = \dfrac{1}{- 20} ⇒ {v}_{A} = \dfrac{- 45 \times ( - 20 )}{- 45 - ( - 20 )} = \dfrac{- 900}{25} ⇒ {v}_{A} = - 36cm$

And~${u}_{B} = - 35cm$

$\dfrac{1}{vB} + \dfrac{1}{uB} = \dfrac{1}{f} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{vB} + \dfrac{1}{- 35} = \dfrac{1}{- 20} ⇒ {v}_{B} = \dfrac{- 35 \times ( - 20 )}{- 35 - ( - 20 )} = \dfrac{700}{- 15} ⇒ {v}_{B} = - \dfrac{140}{3}cm$

Now,~length of image$= {v}_{A} - {v}_{B}$

$= \left(- 36 + \dfrac{140}{3}\right)cm$

$= \dfrac{- 108 + 140}{3}cm$

$= \dfrac{32}{3}cm$

$∴ x = 32$

questions.q: In a compound microscope, the magnified virtual image is formed at a distance of $25\text{cm}$ from the eye-piece. The focal length of its objective lens is $1\text{cm}$. If the magnification is $100$ and the tube length of the microscope is $20\text{cm}$, then the focal length of the eye-piece lens (in $\text{cm}$) is ______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$M = \dfrac{v0}{u0} \left($1 + \dfrac{D}{fe}\right)$

$M = \dfrac{L}{f0} \left($1 + \dfrac{D}{fe}\right)$

$100 = 20 \left(1\right)\left($1 + $\dfrac{25}{fe}\right)~;~$5 = 1 + $\dfrac{25}{fe}

$4 = $\dfrac{25}{fe}~;~${f}_{e} = $\dfrac{25}{4} =$6 .25 cm$

$

questions.q: Light from a point source in air falls on a convex curved surface of radius $20$ cm and refractive index $1 . 5$. If the source is located at $100$ cm from the convex surface, the image will be formed at ______ $cm$ from the object.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{\mu2}{v} - \dfrac{\mu1}{u} = \dfrac{{μ}_{2} - {μ}_{1}}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 .5}{v} - \dfrac{1}{- 100} = \dfrac{1 .5 - 1}{20}$

$⇒ v = 100cm$

Distance from object

$= 100 + 100$

$= 200cm$

questions.q: A small bulb is placed at the bottom of a tank containing water to a depth of $\sqrt{7}m$. The refractive index of water is $\dfrac{4}{3}$. The area of the surface of water through which light from the bulb can emerge out is $x\pim^{2}$. The value of $x$& is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Apply Snell's law,& $\dfrac{sin ⁡ 90 °}{sin ⁡ C} = \mu$

$⇒ sinC = \dfrac{1}{μ} ⇒ \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + h^{2}} = \dfrac{3}{4}$



Squaring, $16R^{2} = 9R^{2} + 9h^{2}$

$⇒ 7R^{2} = 9h^{2} ⇒ R = \dfrac{3}{7}h = \dfrac{3}{7} \times \sqrt{7} = 3m$

The area of the circle is,~$A = \piR^{2} = \pi\left(3\right)2m^{2} ⇒ \alpha = 9$

questions.q:
A thin prism of angle $6 °$~and refractive index for yellow light \left({n}_{Y}\right)1 . 5$~is combined with another prism of angle $5 °$ and ${n}_{Y} = 1 . 55$. The combination produces no dispersion. The net average deviation~ \left(\delta\right)$~produced by the combination is \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) °$. The value of $x$ is _____ .

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for deviation due to a thin prism is given by,& $\delta = A \left(\mu -1\right)$.

Therefore, for prism~$1$:

${δ}_{1} = 6\left(1 . 5 - 1\right) = 3 °$

And for prism~$2$:

${δ}_{2} = - 5\left(1 . 55 - 1\right) = - 2 . 75 °$

$⇒ {δ}_{net} = {δ}_{1} + {δ}_{2} = 3 ° - 2 . 75 ° = 0 . 25 ° = \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)°$

Therefore,~$x = 4.

$

questions.q: A bi convex lens of focal length $10$ cm is cut in two identical parts along a plane perpendicular to the principal axis. The power of each lens after cut is _____ $D$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

The focal& length of the bi-convex lens& \left(f\right)$ can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{f} & = & ( \mu - 1 ) \left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{- R}\right) \\ & = & \dfrac{2\left(\mu - 1\right)}{R} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

When the lens is cut into two halves, the focal length~\left(f '\right)$~of each part can be calculated as follows:

\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{f '}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } ( \mu - 1 ) $\$left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{∞}\right)\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \left(\mu -$1\right)R . . . \left($2\right)\end{cases}$

Hence, the ratio of the powers for both the lenses can be~given by

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{P '}{P}& = & \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{f '}}{\dfrac{1}{f}}\\ & = & \dfrac{f}{f '}\\ & = & \dfrac{\left(\mu - 1\right)R}{\dfrac{2\left(\mu - 1\right)}{R}}\\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}\\ & ⇒ & P ' = \dfrac{P}{2} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the value of the known parameter into equation (3) to calculate the required power.

$\begin{cases}P ' & = & \dfrac{10D}{2}\\ & = & 5D\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: A fish rising vertically upward with a uniform velocity of $8ms^{– 1},$ observes that a bird is diving vertically downward towards the fish with the velocity of $12ms^{– 1} .$ If the refractive index of water is~$\dfrac{4}{3},$ then the~actual velocity of the diving bird to pick the fish, will be__________ms^{- 1} .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the fish be at a depth& $x$~from the surface and let the bird be at height~$y$~from the surface. So, with respect to fish

$y ' = \muy + x ⇒ y ' = \dfrac{4y}{3} + x$

Differentiating with respect to time,

$\dfrac{dy '}{dt} = \dfrac{4dy}{3dt} + \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4y}{3} + \dfrac{dx}{dt} = - 12$

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{3} \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dt} = - 12 + 8 = - 4$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dt} = - 3ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A point object& $O$ is placed in front of two thin symmetrical coaxial convex lenses ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$ with focal length $24$ cm and~$9$ cm respectively. The distance between two lenses is $10$ cm and the object is placed $6$ cm away from lens ${L}_{1}$ as shown in the figure. The distance between the object and the image formed by the system of two lenses is _____________~$cm$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For& ${L}_{1}$:

$\dfrac{1}{v1} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{24}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v1} = \dfrac{1}{24} - \dfrac{1}{6}$

$= \dfrac{1 - 4}{24}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v1} = \left(\dfrac{- 3}{24}\right)

$⇒ {v}_{1} = – 8cm$

For~${L}_{2}$:

$u = – 18cm$

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{18} = \dfrac{1}{9}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{1}{18}

$= $\dfrac{2 - 1}{18}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{18}

$⇒ v = 18cm$

Distance between object and distance~$= 16 + 18 = 34cm$.

$

questions.q: A light ray is incident on a glass slab of thickness $4 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~cm}$ and refractive index $\sqrt{2}$ . The angle of incidence is equal to the critical angle for the glass slab with air. The lateral displacement of ray after passing through glass slab is _____ $\mathrm{cm}$.  \left(\right.$ Given \left.\sin 15^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=0.25\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & i=\theta_c \\ & \Rightarrow i=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\mu}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow i=45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \end{aligned}$ and according to snell's law $\begin{aligned} & 1 \sin 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\sqrt{2} \sin \mathrm{r} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \end{aligned}$
Lateral displacement $\Delta=\frac{\mathrm{t} \sin (\mathrm{i}-\mathrm{r})}{\cos \mathrm{r}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \Delta=\frac{4 \sqrt{3} \times \sin 15^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}}{\cos 30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \Delta=2 \mathrm{~cm} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The distance between object and its two times magnified real image as produced by a convex lens is $45$ cm. The focal length of the lens used is ________cm.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnification, $m = \dfrac{v}{u} = - 2$

$⇒ v = - 2u \ldots \left(i\right)$

As,

$v - u = 45 \ldots \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ u = - 15cm$

Then, $v = 30cm$

From lens equation, we can write

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}⇒ \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{30} -1 \left(-15\right)$

$⇒ f = + 10cm

$
